slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Graphs
slides.narration: Let's solve Two Edge Connected Graph, a very hard graphs problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Undirected adjacency list; is the graph connected and free of bridges (stays connected after removing any single edge)?
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Undirected adjacency list; is the graph connected and free of bridges (stays connected after removing any single edge)? Empty graph counts as true. Tarjan low-link.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: A graph has no bridges if every DFS subtree has a back edge reaching above its root.
slides.narration: A graph has no bridges if every DFS subtree has a back edge reaching above its root.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. Compute the lowest reachable arrival time
3. A child with low time above the parent is a bridge
slides.narration: Step by step. First, dFS with arrival times. Second, compute the lowest reachable arrival time. Third, a child with low time above the parent is a bridge. Fourth, check connectivity too.
